title: Experimental origin of animal multicellular development

concept.text: The proposed innovation is to construct a stable, differentiated multicellular life cycle in a unicellular relative of animals by introducing a specified set of genetic and cellular changes. Starting with a documented unicellular holozoan baseline, such as a suitable choanoflagellate, the resulting lineage would repeatedly develop from one founding cell into an organized multicellular body whose different cell types perform complementary functions. Reproduction would depend on completing that multicellular life cycle, although each generation could begin as a single cell. This is a proposed experimental capability, not an achievement reported in the supplied sources.

The central question is sufficiency: which changes, in a particular biological background, can make this integrated developmental system work? Many molecular components associated with animal multicellularity existed before animals, and living relatives already exhibit colonies, differentiation or embryo-like development. Those observations identify possible starting materials and mechanisms. The proposed construction would connect them into a newly established, heritable life cycle with organized division of labor. Here, animal-like developmental organization describes the experimental target; it does not imply that the resulting organism would be taxonomically an animal.

significance.text: In nearly all animals, the multicellular body is established through successive divisions of a single founding cell, accompanied by regulated morphogenesis and differentiation. Comparative genomics and studies of choanoflagellates, filastereans and ichthyosporeans help reconstruct how this organization could have arisen. A successful construction would add a major causal result: an experimentally demonstrated set of changes sufficient to generate stable, differentiated multicellular development in a chosen modern organism. Its direct products would be the constructed lineage and a reproducible account of the interventions that produce its life cycle.

The historical interpretation would remain bounded. Animals share common ancestry, but the timing and assembly of individual developmental components remain uncertain; similar components in a distant relative may reflect ancient conservation or convergence. Engineering one successful route would therefore establish a possible mechanism in a modern biological background. It would not establish that animals actually evolved by that route, that every introduced change was necessary, or that the intervention set was minimal. It would also not automatically explain the Cambrian radiation, generate a bilaterian, or confer animal taxonomic identity.

Conditional synthesis: once a reproducible construction existed, it could provide a tractable system for testing how developmental coordination becomes stable, how cells acquire complementary roles, and which ecological conditions favor dependence on a multicellular body. Such downstream uses would require further experiments. Success in one lineage would not establish a general recipe applicable to all unicellular organisms or explain every independent origin of multicellularity.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unresolved capability is a controlled construction that links a specified intervention to obligatory multicellular reproduction, reproducible development and functional differentiation. Possessing ancestral adhesion, signaling or extracellular-matrix components does not by itself show how those components can be coordinated into such a life cycle. Brunet and King's 2017 review described much of the evidence bearing on proposed origins of differentiation as descriptive and concentrated on a few candidate genes. That establishes a mechanistic gap at the review's date; the supplied materials do not establish whether the proposed construction remained unreported throughout the field as of 1 November 2026.

Engineering synthesis: the practical challenge is to coordinate cell proliferation, attachment, spatial organization, cell-fate regulation and reproduction so that they reliably produce a functioning multicellular organism. Different cell forms must contribute complementary functions, and the lineage must transmit the developmental capacity across complete reproductive cycles. These are coupled requirements: stable clustering alone does not demonstrate development, and distinguishable cell morphologies alone do not demonstrate integrated division of labor.

A further barrier is distinguishing a newly constructed capability from an existing facultative colony or natural developmental stage. The associated Nature peer-review exchange notes that Salpingoeca rosetta colonies can remain stable and propagate by fission while an inducing signal is present. Consequently, persistence alone is insufficient to distinguish the proposed advance. Conversely, removal of one inducing cue would test a particular form of developmental autonomy, not independence from nutrients, suitable culture conditions or all environmental regulation. Establishing whether sponges or ctenophores diverged first would constrain evolutionary history but would not itself supply a sufficient developmental mechanism.

current_state.text: In their review published on 23 October 2017 in Developmental Cell, Thibaut Brunet and Nicole King described animal multicellularity and spatial differentiation as likely elaborations of older cellular components during the animal stem lineage. Many relevant signaling, adhesion and extracellular-matrix components predate animals. Their account supports the biological plausibility of assembling new organization from an older molecular toolkit, while retaining uncertainty about the actual evolutionary steps. It is a comparative and mechanistic synthesis, not a report of constructing the proposed lineage.

In a Nature paper published on 6 November 2024, Marine Olivetta and colleagues reported a natural developmental program in Chromosphaera perkinsii, an ichthyosporean whose lineage diverged from animals roughly a billion years ago. The abstract describes symmetry breaking followed by cleavage divisions that produce a prolonged multicellular colony with distinct coexisting cell types. This demonstrates relevant developmental features outside animals. It does not report engineering a unicellular organism into the proposed obligately multicellular lineage. The authors leave ancient conservation and convergent evolution as alternative explanations for the resemblance to animal development.

The associated peer-review exchange provides useful qualifications about differentiation in C. perkinsii. Initial concerns about cell-type interpretation were followed by additional cell tracking and morphological observations. The authors argued that flagellated and proliferative cells have different morphologies and fates at cell release, while retaining uncertainty about developmental trajectories and lacking cell-type-resolved transcriptomics. They also acknowledged that the different cell types had not been shown to function together in the coordinated manner associated with complex multicellular organisms. These limits narrow what the result establishes; they do not negate the reported coexistence of distinct cell types.

The supplied review had the complete main text of the 2017 review, but did not inspect its linked supplements or figure images. For the 2024 study, the retained Nature HTML was a partial subscription preview supporting the abstract-level findings. Its figures and videos were not inspected. The retained PDFs were a reporting summary and a peer-review file, rather than the complete research article. Successful text extraction therefore did not provide complete access to the experimental report, and the supplied review cannot serve as an independent audit of all of its results.

Evidence-scope synthesis: the texts assessed in the supplied review do not report the proposed engineered lineage. However, no bounded freshness search was supplied, so they do not establish the field-wide absence of such a construction as of 1 November 2026. The supported conclusion is that the documented studies provide important precursor biology and historical hypotheses; the present-day availability of the full proposed capability remains unresolved by this evidence set.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed benchmark: begin with a documented unicellular holozoan baseline and specify the genetic and cellular changes introduced. The resulting lineage should reproduce through at least 100 complete organismal generations, with each generation developing clonally from one founding cell through a reproducible developmental program. During the multicellular phase, it should maintain at least two spatially organized cell types with demonstrated division of labor. The numerical thresholds are proposed experimental benchmarks, not established standards or a definition of an animal.
completion_criteria.label: Clonal development sustains differentiated multicellularity for 100 complete organismal generations

completion_criteria.text: Proposed operational boundaries: a single-cell founding stage is compatible with obligatory multicellularity, but a self-sustaining free-living unicellular reproductive cycle would not satisfy this benchmark. The multicellular life cycle should persist after removal of the particular inducing cue under otherwise permissive culture conditions. An unchanged pre-existing multicellular stage would not demonstrate construction of the target capability, and a transient induced colony would not suffice. An ichthyosporean should therefore not qualify merely because its unmodified life cycle already includes multicellular development; the baseline and newly introduced capabilities must be distinguished.
completion_criteria.label: Newly constructed obligatory multicellularity persists without the inducing cue

completion_criteria.text: Proposed convincing evidence: document complete life cycles by lineage tracking, show reproducible spatial organization and cell fates, and demonstrate complementary cell functions through functional measurements or perturbations. Matched ancestral and intervention controls should establish which phenotype depends on the introduced changes. Independent reconstructions and replication by another laboratory would strengthen the sufficiency claim. Reversal or omission experiments could test necessity within the engineered system, but necessity and minimality would require evidence beyond successful construction alone.
completion_criteria.label: Tracked development and functional measurements establish phenotypes with matched controls

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical reporting: state the culture conditions, developmental failure rates, stability of the introduced changes and any dependence on continued selection or external manipulation. Passing a finite set of tests would establish the demonstrated breadth and persistence of the phenotype under those conditions. It would not establish literal universality, reconstruct the actual ancestral sequence, or settle the organism's taxonomic identity.
completion_criteria.label: Report experimental conditions, phenotype reliability, and limits of inference

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: ZOO-01, “A fertile animal booted from a chemically synthesized genome,” overlaps in constructing a heritable biological system, but asks whether a synthesized genome can initiate an animal life cycle. ZOO-08 asks how specified changes can establish multicellular development in a unicellular relative and does not require whole-genome synthesis. ZOO-10, “Fertile adulthood from a vertebrate cell line, with no gestational parent,” likewise concerns development from cells, but starts with an existing vertebrate developmental system rather than constructing the transition to multicellular organization.

Roster-based synthesis: ZOO-09, “A heritable body plan the ancestor never had,” shares an interest in new developmental organization, but its defining target is a novel inherited body plan rather than the origin of an obligatory multicellular life cycle. ZOO-02, “Complete limb regeneration in an adult mammal,” concerns restoring organized anatomy within an already multicellular animal. Both would involve developmental control, while addressing different starting states and outcomes from ZOO-08.

Roster-based synthesis: ZOO-03, “Negligible senescence as an installed life-history program,” ZOO-06, “A germline-transmitted photosynthetic organelle in an animal,” and ZOO-07, “Reversible whole-animal biostasis,” concern major changes to the life history, metabolism or physiological state of an existing animal. Their overlap with ZOO-08 lies in coordinating cellular behavior at organismal scale. None, by its supplied identity, requires constructing animal-like multicellular development from a unicellular relative.

Roster-based synthesis: ZOO-04, “Self-sustaining populations reconstructed from extinct animal species,” shares the requirement for heritable reproductive continuity, but targets restoration of an extinct animal lineage and population. ZOO-05, “Two-way semantic communication with another animal species,” concerns communication with existing animals and has little direct mechanistic overlap with the construction proposed here. These remain separate innovations with distinct demonstrations of success.

brief.title: Building a body from a single-celled relative of animals
possible: Researchers could give a single-celled relative of animals a heritable life cycle in which each founding cell grows into an organized body. Different cell types would share the work, and reproduction would depend on completing that body's development.
why: This would turn a question about animal origins into an experiment: which changes can make cells develop and reproduce as a coordinated body? Biologists would gain a working organism and a reproducible recipe for studying that transition.

sources.showed: Their review describes how many molecular components used for animal development existed before animals. It sets out possible routes by which cells acquired different roles.
sources.cited_for: Animal development could have arisen by changing how older cellular components work together.
sources.not_established: The review does not demonstrate changes sufficient to construct a body with complementary cell functions and a heritable life cycle.

sources.showed: They found that single cells of Chromosphaera perkinsii, a relative of animals, naturally divide into lasting colonies containing distinct cell types.
sources.quote: undergo symmetry breaking and develop through cleavage divisions to produce a prolonged multicellular colony with distinct co-existing cell types.
sources.cited_for: A living relative of animals already has a natural developmental program that produces different cell types together.
sources.not_established: The study does not construct a new life cycle or establish that the different cell types perform coordinated, complementary functions.

shown: Marine Olivetta and colleagues found natural development resembling aspects of early animal development in Chromosphaera perkinsii. A founding cell divides into a lasting colony with distinct cell types. This provides a possible starting point for understanding how organized bodies arise.
missing: A controlled construction must connect specified changes to a newly established life cycle that requires a multicellular body for reproduction.
Different cell types must demonstrably perform complementary jobs in reproducible spatial arrangements.
The constructed life cycle must pass reliably between generations and persist after its particular triggering signal is removed.

milestones.label: Organized development lasts 100 generations
milestones.explanation: A documented single-celled starting organism with specified changes would have to repeatedly develop from a founding cell into a body with spatially organized cell types sharing tasks. This would establish inherited development.

milestones.label: Body-dependent reproduction persists after the trigger is removed
milestones.explanation: The newly constructed life cycle would have to persist without its triggering signal, with reproduction requiring the body stage. This would distinguish it from a temporary colony or an unchanged natural stage.

milestones.label: Tracked cells and controlled tests establish shared functions
milestones.explanation: Cell tracking and functional tests with matched controls would have to connect the introduced changes to reproducible development and complementary cell roles. This would establish what the changes actually cause.

milestones.label: Conditions, reliability and limits are reported
milestones.explanation: Experiments would have to report culture conditions, failure rates, genetic stability and dependence on continued selection or manipulation. This would define where the life cycle works and how reliably it persists.

uncertain: Similar development in animals and their relatives could reflect ancient inheritance or separate evolutionary origins.
A successful construction would establish a possible route, while leaving the actual evolutionary route and the smallest necessary set of changes open.
The proposed generation count and minimum variety of cell types need experimental justification as measures of success.

page.title: Synthetic multicellular development in non-animal holozoans
page.definition: A constructed non-animal holozoan, a unicellular relative of animals, repeatedly develops from one cell into a body with regulated shape and spatially organized cell types performing complementary functions. Its heritable life cycle requires the multicellular phase for reproduction.

goal.need: Animal multicellularity arose more than 600 million years ago; animal bodies coordinate thousands to billions of cells. Many adhesion and signalling components predate animals. NSF announced a synthetic-multicellularity prize on 8 October 2026. Reconstructing development in an animal relative tests which changes suffice to organize this inherited machinery into a reproducing body.

statements.body: U.S. National Science Foundation, Grand Research Challenge on Synthetic Multicellularity
statements.quote: In such a system, a previously unicellular organism is modified with the ability to develop into multiple, functionally distinct cells.
statements.context: The programme concerns engineered organisms generally; its published description does not require a holozoan host or obligate multicellular reproduction.

statements.body: Institut de Biologia Evolutiva research team: Ruiz-Trillo, Casacuberta, Brown and Solé
statements.quote: Inspired by this engineering perspective, experimentalists can attempt to reconstruct ancestral states in living unicellular relatives—such as Capsaspora—by targeted modification.
statements.context: A research proposal in the investigators' review of animal origins.

completion.title: Specified changes reconstruct an obligate, differentiated holozoan developmental life cycle.
completion.criterion: Starting from a documented non-animal holozoan baseline, specified changes produce a heritable life cycle that repeatedly develops clonally from one founding cell into a body with regulated morphology and spatially organized cell types performing complementary functions. Reproduction requires the multicellular phase. Reconstruction and comparison with the baseline establish that the changes suffice to produce this integration. A single-cell founding stage is compatible with the test.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis of the NSF engineering goal and published biological definitions; no external body was found to have adopted this combined construction test.
completion.basis: Searches of NSF challenge and prize documentation, academy material, and published multicellularity definitions found no combined construction test for obligate holozoan development. NSF specifies engineered functional differentiation but supplies no detailed stage thresholds. This Atlas test combines that goal with published criteria for obligate reproduction, differentiated cell types and regulated body form.

milestones.title: A non-animal holozoan forms a multicellular body by division of one founding cell.
milestones.criterion: Daughter cells remain attached through successive divisions, producing a clonal multicellular structure. Fairclough and colleagues reported this in Salpingoeca rosetta on 26 October 2010: colonies contained 4 to about 50 cells, and time-lapse observations lasted at least 12 hours. Cell-division inhibition prevented colony formation in assays using three replicate cultures; removal restored it.
milestones.set_by: The field's clonal-development convention, stated by Brunet and King in their 2017 review and applied experimentally by Fairclough and colleagues in 2010.
milestones.threshold_quote: serial cell division without separation of sister cells

milestones.title: A non-animal holozoan body contains cell types distinguished by morphology and gene expression.
milestones.criterion: Coexisting cells in a multicellular structure have recurrent identities defined jointly by morphology and gene-expression profile, under gene-regulatory control. Olivetta and colleagues reported distinct coexisting morphologies in Chromosphaera perkinsii on 6 November 2024. Post-release growth measurements followed five flagellated and five proliferative cells over 10 minutes. Those measurements supply morphological evidence; they do not establish cell-type-resolved expression profiles.
milestones.set_by: Ros-Rocher and colleagues, Open Biology, 2021, Box 1: their working definition of a cell type in animal-origins research.
milestones.threshold_quote: a classification unit based on the combined observations of a cell morphology and gene expression profile

milestones.title: Specialized cell types raise a holozoan body's fitness through complementary tasks.
milestones.criterion: Cells specialize in complementary cooperative tasks, and the multicellular group gains a fitness benefit from their interaction compared with groups containing only one of the constituent cell types. The comparison distinguishes collective benefit from individual adaptation to local conditions. This published division-of-labour criterion was formulated for microbial biofilms; it specifies no universal numerical effect-size cutoff.
milestones.set_by: Van Gestel, Vlamakis and Kolter, Microbiology Spectrum, 2015, section on division of labour; the operational comparison was formulated for bacterial biofilms.
milestones.threshold_quote: a colony that consists of multiple cell types performs better than a colony that consists solely of any one of them.

milestones.title: A non-animal holozoan has an obligate multicellular life cycle with differentiated cells and regulated form.
milestones.criterion: A developmentally regulated body containing different cell types is an obligatory part of the lineage's reproductive life cycle. Descendants repeat this organization. Single-cell propagules can found new bodies, but isolated cells cannot maintain an autonomous unicellular reproductive cycle under the tested conditions. This establishes the complex-multicellularity phenotype; completion additionally requires its construction through specified changes from a documented baseline.
milestones.set_by: The complex-multicellularity convention stated by Brunet and King in 2017, citing Knoll; obligacy follows the definition published by Fisher and Regenberg in 2019.
milestones.threshold_quote: obligate multicellularity with different cell types and regulated organismal morphology

not_found: No externally adopted combined acceptance test or detailed NSF prize-stage criteria was found for constructing obligate development in a non-animal holozoan.
No numerical generation-count, reliability or cue-withdrawal threshold was found for this construction.
No published construction satisfying the combined completion criterion was found.

results.finding: One C. perkinsii cell underwent successive cleavage divisions to form a multicellular colony.
results.detail: The abstract reports that single cells develop through cleavage divisions into multicellular colonies; Supplementary Video 4 documents one such cell.

Time-lapse of a Plasma Membrane-stained (PM)

results.finding: C. perkinsii colonies contained flagellated and non-flagellated cells; five cells of each type were measured after release.
results.detail: The observations distinguish morphologies and growth behavior, but the reported transcriptomics do not establish expression profiles for each coexisting cell type or their gene-regulatory control.

results.finding: Two synchronized C. perkinsii cells were followed through a life cycle ending in release of newborn cells.
results.detail: The paper also reports multicellular colonies with coexisting cell types, but the supplied text does not establish that isolated cells cannot sustain unicellular reproduction under the tested conditions.
